31.0.0.en: 1 Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the LORD! 2 Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words: but will arise against the house of the evildoers, and against the help of them that work iniquity. 3 Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the LORD shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together.

31.0.1.en: The prophet Isaiah presents to us a wonderful spiritual thought, for the matter of resorting to Pharaoh is not merely a political and military plan but a theological matter that touches the life of man and his eternal destiny. He who leans on men, however great their number, their resources, or their strength [1], clings to carnal, mortal people and becomes mortal like them, while he who clings to the Savior, the Holy One of Israel, the unchangeable, the eternal, carries immortality with him. Our reliance on men unites us with them and we perish; our reliance on God binds us to Him and we share His eternal glories. This is what he meant when he warned them, saying: "Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the LORD shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together" [3].

31.0.2.en: Let us then lean on the eternal Creator, not on the weak creature that is unable even to help itself.

31.0.4.en: Now, through a kind of weakness of the human soul, when a man falls into distress he despairs of God, choosing to lean on a man.

31.0.5.en: Let someone say to a man fallen into distress: "There is a great man who will set you free," and at once he smiles and rejoices and his spirits rise; but if it is said to him, "God will set you free," he falls into a state of discouragement and despair!

31.0.6.en: You rejoice when you receive help from a mortal; how then do you grieve when you receive help from the Creator?!

31.0.7.en: You have received a promise that one who himself needs to be set free will set you free, and your spirits rise like one who has received great help. Here you receive a promise from the One (God) who sets free, who needs no one to set Him free, and yet you despair as though you had received a feeble thing.

31.0.8.en: Woe to such thoughts! They have gone astray; truly a grievous and sorrowful death has come upon them!

31.0.9.en: * "His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish" (Ps 146:4)...

31.0.10.en: "I have seen the wicked in great power, exalted above the cedars of Lebanon. Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found" (Ps 37:35-36)...

31.0.11.en: All these are subject to death, quickly passing, perishing.

31.0.12.en: Then what must we do if we do not hope in the sons of men nor in princes? What must we do? "Blessed is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help" (Ps 146:5), whose help is not this man or that man, nor this angel or that angel, but "blessed is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help." For Jacob had a great helper, who thus raised up Israel from Jacob. What a mighty help! Now he is Israel, "who sees God"! If you also remain here and do not wander away from the vision of God, if the God of Jacob becomes your helper, then you are changed from Jacob into Israel; you see God, and troubles and all sighs come to an end, confusions cease, and happy songs of praise take their place...

31.0.13.en: Let your hope be in the Lord your God, let your hope be in Him.

31.1.s.en: 2. God, the protector of His children:

31.1.0.en: 4 For thus hath the LORD spoken unto me, Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the LORD of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof. 5 As birds flying, so will the LORD of hosts defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver it; and sparing he will preserve it.

31.1.1.en: If the enemy of good, the devil, is like a roaring lion who wants to devour in order to eat and be satisfied and destroy his prey (1 Pet 5:8), then "the Holy One of Israel" is the Lion that came out of the tribe of Judah (Rev 5:5), who does not destroy the prey but is able to protect it. He acquires the soul as prey, surrounding it, to give it His royal traits, so He makes His believers "priests and kings" (Rev 1:6), giving them His immortality and a share in His glories.

31.2.0.en: God is a trustworthy refuge, able to protect us and also to shepherd us; therefore He likens Himself to the lion, the king of the beasts, before whom no one can stand, and at the same time to a bird that cares for its young [5].

31.2.1.en: Our Christ shepherds us on the Cross as a lion who couched and lay down (Gen 49:9), and the enemy was not able to approach Him, nor to approach us.

31.3.s.en: 3. A call to return to God:

31.3.0.en: 6 Turn ye unto him from whom the children of Israel have deeply revolted. 7 For in that day every man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made unto you for a sin. 8 Then shall the Assyrian fall with the sword, not of a mighty man; and the sword, not of a mean man, shall devour him: but he shall flee from the sword, and his chosen ones shall be under tribute. 9 And his rock shall pass away for fear, and his princes shall be afraid of the ensign, saith the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.

31.3.1.en: The prophet reveals the purpose of God's work with them, for the Lord shatters Assyria in a way that is neither human nor natural, not to display His divine power but to draw the souls of those who deny Him, for the Lord says: "Turn ye unto him from whom the children of Israel have deeply revolted... Then shall the Assyrian fall with the sword, not of a mighty man; and the sword, not of a mean man, shall devour him..." [6, 8].

31.3.2.en: Is this not a picture of God's salvation accomplished on the Cross, where He brought down the devil not by human thought nor by a material sword but by giving His life as a sin offering for us, and a burnt offering of love on our behalf and in our name, so that the enemy was crushed under our feet and we returned to God with new depths that the men of the Old Testament did not experience as we have?!

32.0.s.en: 1. The blessings of the Kingdom of Christ:

32.0.0.en: 1 Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment. 2 And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land. 3 And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken. 4 The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly. 5 The vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the crafty one said to be noble. 6 For the vile person will speak villany, and his heart will work iniquity, to practise hypocrisy, and to utter error against the LORD, to make empty the soul of the hungry, and he will cause the drink of the thirsty to fail. 7 The instruments also of the crafty one are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right. 8 But the liberal deviseth liberal things; and by liberal things shall he stand.

32.0.1.en: The talk here concerns a flourishing kingdom. Some scholars see that it is the kingdom of Hezekiah, which began with spiritual and social reform, although many reformed only the outward form; others see that the talk here is about the Lord Christ, because the blessings mentioned here were not fulfilled in the days of Hezekiah; but a third group sees that it is about King Hezekiah or other kings as a shadow of the Lord Christ.

32.0.2.en: What does Christ the King offer us?

32.0.3.en: A. A constitution of justice and truth: "Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment" [1]. If the Lord reigned on the wood, that is, through the Cross, and paid the price of our sins in fulfillment of justice, then He sets up His disciples and believers as rulers, so that we exercise our spiritual authority not over others but over our souls, our feelings, our emotions, and our faculties, not by suppressing or destroying them but "in judgment," that is, by sanctifying them in Christ the Truth.

32.0.4.en: B. Instead of troubles and afflictions, this King becomes "an hiding place from the wind," protecting the believers from the winds of trials and bitter pressures; "and a covert from the tempest," that is, like a shelter or covering that protects them from the sweeping waters; "as rivers of water in a dry place," that is, He waters the thirsty souls in the barren wilderness; "as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land," they hide in Christ the Rock, so that no harm touches them.

32.0.5.en: Thus he presents four similes for the work of the Lord Christ in the life of His believers: a hiding place, a covert, rivers of water, a great rock.

32.0.6.en: Through these similes the prophet sees us as like a traveler who finds in the Lord Christ all his needs: when violent storms blow upon him he finds in Him the faithful refuge; if sweeping floods overtake him he finds Him a protective covering; if he suffers thirst the Lord becomes for him rivers of living water; and if the whole world is stirred up he takes shelter in Him as a solid rock able to hide him and protect him even from death.

32.0.7.en: That is, God the Savior offers Himself as everything to His believers so that they lack nothing. He has presented Himself through many names so that we may realize that He is the secret of our true satisfaction, and as St. John Chrysostom says:

32.0.8.en: [Why is He called the Way? That we may understand that through Him we meet the Father. Why is He called the Rock? That we may understand that He is the keeper and establisher of the faith.

32.0.9.en: Why is He called the Fountain? That we may understand that He is the source of everything.

32.0.10.en: Why is He called the Root? That we may understand that in Him is the power of growth.

32.0.11.en: Why is He called the Shepherd? Because He shepherds us.

32.0.12.en: Why is He called the Lamb? Because He was offered as a ransom for us and became an offering.

32.0.13.en: Why is He called the Life? Because He raised us up when we were dead.

32.0.14.en: Why is He called the Light? Because He rescued us from the darkness.

32.0.15.en: Why is He called the Arm? Because He is of one essence with the Father.

32.0.16.en: Why is He called the Word? Because He is begotten of the Father; as my word is begotten of me, so also the Son is begotten of the Father.

32.0.17.en: Why is He called our Garment? Because I clothed myself with Him when I was baptized.

32.0.18.en: Why is He called the Table? Because I am nourished on Him when I partake of the Mysteries.

32.0.19.en: Why is He called the House? Because I dwell in Him.

32.0.20.en: Why is He called the Bridegroom? Because He received me as His bride.

32.0.21.en: Why is He called Undefiled? Because He took me as a virgin.

32.0.22.en: Why is He called the Master? Because I am His servant.

32.0.23.en: If you hear these things, I beg you not to understand them in a material sense, but soar high with your mind, for they are not to be taken in a bodily sense].

32.0.24.en: * Blessed is he who has forgotten the talk of the world through his talk with You, for from You all his needs are fulfilled. You are his food and drink! You are his house and his dwelling of rest; to You he enters at all times to take cover! You are his sun and his day; by Your light he sees hidden things. You are the Father who begot him! You gave him the Spirit of Your Son in his heart!

32.1.0.en: The Spiritual Elder C. The Lord Christ offers His believers spiritual insight to see the unseen things, so that their inner eyes may not be darkened: "the eyes of them that see shall not be dim (darkened)" [3]. He also gives us the ability to listen to His commandment and to hearken to His words with joy: "and the ears of them that hear shall hearken" [3]. He offers wisdom with understanding and knowledge: "the heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge" [4]. He gives the tongue fitting and effective speech: "and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly." And finally He gives us the grace of discernment, so that we do not count the vile person liberal nor the crafty one noble [5].

32.1.1.en: In short, He gives: inner insight, hearing with obedience, wisdom with understanding and knowledge, the ability to speak constructively, the grace of discernment. All this is accomplished by the Savior, who removes the sin that causes blindness, disobedience, folly, inability to speak the truth, and lack of discernment.

32.1.2.en: * My God... You are my light! Open my eyes that they may behold Your divine splendor, that I may be able to walk in my way without stumbling in the snares of the enemy...

32.1.3.en: You are the light for the children of light! Your day knows no sunset! Your day shines for Your children so that they do not stumble!

32.1.4.en: But those who are outside of You walk in darkness and live in it...!

32.1.5.en: Yes, outside Your radiance truth flees from me and error draws near to me; conceit fills me, and truth flees from me! I fall into confusion instead of discernment; ignorance becomes mine instead of knowledge, blindness instead of insight; I no longer have a way that leads to life...

32.2.0.en: St. Augustine D. God distinguishes between the vile and the liberal, for He is the searcher of hearts and the knower of hidden things [6-8].

32.3.0.en: 9 Rise up, ye women that are at ease; hear my voice, ye careless daughters; give ear unto my speech. 10 For days beyond a year shall ye tremble, ye careless women: for the vintage shall fail, the gathering shall not come. 11 Tremble, ye women that are at ease; be troubled, ye careless ones: strip you, and make you bare, and gird yourselves upon the loins. 12 They shall smite upon the breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine. 13 Upon the land of my people shall come up thorns and briers; yea, upon all the houses of joy in the joyous city: 14 Because the palaces shall be forsaken; the multitude of the city shall be left; the forts and towers shall be for dens for ever, a joy of wild asses, a pasture of flocks;

32.3.1.en: After speaking about the blessings of the Kingdom of Christ, among them the distinction between the vile and the liberal, God knowing how to judge the first and honor the second, he began to speak to us about the judgment of the vile person in the form of an address to the pampered, luxurious women who go out after the harvest to spend periods of play together in temporal joy and in an unseemly, carnal manner. There is no longer a feast of harvest, for the enemy seizes all the crops.

32.3.2.en: These women represent those who refuse to believe in the Lord Christ, who walk outside His spiritual Kingdom, and they are afflicted with the following:

32.4.0.en: A. Instead of tranquility and peace they tremble [11]...

32.4.1.en: * Be all my happiness, O You who are wholly good... By You I stand and without You I perish..! By You I am filled with joy, and without You I perish with sorrow...

32.4.2.en: Ah! Make haste and make my soul a dwelling for You, and my heart a resting place... Your fragrance restores my strength, and the remembrance of You eases my pains, Your appearing is my satisfaction (Ps 17:10)!

32.4.3.en: O Life of my soul... my heart runs after You, and melts at the remembrance of Your goodness! When will the time come for my departure to Your Kingdom?! When shall I be granted to behold Your beauty, O Life, the happiness of my heart!

32.4.4.en: Why do You hide Your face from me, O sole happiness of my soul?!

32.4.5.en: Where do You hide, O Lord of beauty, O end of all my aspirations...

32.4.6.en: Draw my heart, for You are my joy!

32.4.7.en: St. Augustine B. Instead of wearing costly garments they strip and make themselves bare and gird upon the loins [11], a sign of the withdrawal of grace and the loss of spiritual covering.

32.4.8.en: What are these costly garments that the human soul wears but the person of the Lord Christ, who hides us in Himself and covers us with His blood and gives us His beauty. As St. Paul says: "For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ" (Gal 3:27). In the waters of Baptism we put on the Lord Christ, and so we bear His righteousness and His glory and His splendor in us. As Mar Jacob of Serugh says: [Baptism is the robe of glory given to Adam, which the serpent stole from him among the trees... Come (O soul) and put on majesty, and acquire light through the pure waters. Come, go down, and put on the garments that divinity has woven, and go up and show us your immortal beauty, that we may rejoice with you... You have put on the many-colored garment like the high priest in the house of purification. Fire and the Spirit weave for you the robe that is all light. O daughter of the peoples, betrothed to the light within the waters].

32.5.0.en: C. Instead of joy they smite upon the breast, lamenting like those who have a dead one [12]; for by their separation from God, the source of life, their souls lost life.

32.5.1.en: * How wretched I am! My God... when will this corrupt nature leave me, and Your perfect power work in me...?! I am Your creature, and behold, I am dying! I am the work of Your hands, and behold, I am descending toward nothingness...! Shall I command the dead man to come out of the grave...! Ah! O my God! I will cry out before I perish, or at least cry out lest I perish, that I may deserve to dwell in You... Support me, O eternal glory, O my joy, reveal Yourself to me, O my God, that I may love it!

32.5.2.en: St. Augustine D. Instead of rejoicing in the harvest, the earth brings forth for them thorns and briers (Isa 3:13), a sign of the coming of the curse with spiritual dryness.

32.6.0.en: E. Their palaces are demolished and the cities are forsaken, and the houses of joy and the joyous city turn into a wilderness with thorns and briers [13-14].

32.6.1.en: F. The hill and the tower turn into perpetual dens in which wild asses (a symbol of the fierce demons) and flocks (animal thoughts) graze.

32.6.2.en: These are the marks of the soul outside Christ: trembling, sorrow, dryness, ruin, and destruction come upon it, so it becomes a dwelling for wicked, beastly spirits and for animal thoughts and lusts.

32.7.0.en: 15 Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness be a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be counted for a forest. 16 Then truth shall dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness remain in the fruitful field. 17 And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever. 18 And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places; 19 When it shall hail, coming down on the forest; and the city shall be low in a low place. 20 Blessed are ye that sow beside all waters, that send forth thither the feet of the ox and the ass.

32.7.1.en: God, in His love, seeks His children for Himself in order to remove from them trembling, bitterness, dryness, and destruction, so He pours out His Holy Spirit upon us that the enemy of good and the thoughts and lusts of the flesh may find no place in us, for it is said: "Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness be a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be counted for a forest" [15].

32.7.2.en: Many commentators see that what is mentioned here points to the descent of the Holy Spirit on the Feast of Pentecost, when the barren wilderness of the soul is turned into a garden bearing the fruits of the Holy Spirit that gladden God and men, while those who deny lose even their natural fruit, so that their weak garden becomes a forest.

32.7.3.en: The prophet depicts for us this Pentecostal work in the life of the Church, saying:

32.8.0.en: "Then truth shall dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness remain in the fruitful field" [16], meaning that the Holy Spirit turns our wilderness into a garden or a paradise in which the Lord Christ, who is the Truth and the Righteousness, dwells. If our Christ promised the gift of the Spirit, then the work of the Spirit in the believer is to prepare him for the indwelling of Christ in him, and the establishing of His Kingdom within us.

32.9.0.en: "And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation" [18]. By the dwelling of the Lord of glory in the midst of His people, peace comes to the midst of the people; our Christ is revealed in us and we dwell in Him, for He is our eternal peace. His peace reigns in our hearts (Col 3:15), so we live in reconciliation with God and men also, and are counted as those who are in heaven itself.

32.10.0.en: Finally the prophet pronounces blessed those who enjoy the gift of the Spirit through the waters of Baptism: "Blessed are ye that sow beside all waters, that send forth thither the feet of the ox and the ass" [20]. It is as though he who sows by the streams of the waters of the Holy Spirit bears an abundant harvest, so the oxen and the asses do not cease carrying it turn after turn, and the feet of these animals pass freely and repeatedly...

32.10.1.en: * Blessed is he who sows beside the waters, for this soul is plowed and watered and trodden by the ox and the ass after it had been dry without rain [20] and humbled without cause. Blessed is he who was the "valley (of Shittim)" (Jn 3:18) watered from the house of the Lord, so that it becomes fresh and produces food for man instead of dryness and unfruitfulness... Therefore it is fitting for us to take care not to lose grace.
